## The framework

:::: {.grid}

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
::: {.etv-card}
[Extract]{.step-pill .pill-e}

### Bring the data in
From a CSV file or straight out of a Wikipedia table. One package each.

`readr::read_csv()` · `htmltab::htmltab()`
:::
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
::: {.etv-card}
[Transform]{.step-pill .pill-t}

### Reshape it to the question
Keep what matters, fix what's broken, group and summarise. Always with `|>`.

`select()` · `filter()` · `mutate()` · `group_by()` · `summarise()`
:::
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
::: {.etv-card}
[Visualize]{.step-pill .pill-v}

### Draw the answer
One clearly labeled chart whose title states the finding, not the variables.

`ggplot() + geom_col() + labs(title = "the answer")`
:::
:::

| 0:10–0:35 | [02 · Café orders: a complete ETV cycle](qmd/02_csv_extract_transform_visualize.qmd) | One question: *which drink category makes the most money, and is it volume or price?* Extract with `read_csv()`, fix a price column stored as text, group and summarise, draw two bar charts, interpret in plain language. |
| 0:35–0:55 | [03 · Wikipedia tables and AI-assisted flows](qmd/03_wikipedia_and_ai_etv_flows.qmd) | Pull the top-50 highest-grossing films table out of Wikipedia with `htmltab()`, clean it, count films per decade. Then the AI loop: question → plan → code → checks → chart → interpretation, with a prompt template and a planted mistake to find. |
| 0:55–1:00 | 03 | Exit task and wrap-up |

## Data

Both files are inside the zip. Download them separately here if you only need one.

:::: {.grid}

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
::: {.etv-card}
### [cafe_orders.csv](data/cafe_orders.csv) · used in 02
**Synthetic.** Four simulated weeks of orders at a fictional campus café (Sept 21 – Oct 18, 2026). No real business. 506 rows, 10 columns. The `price` column is stored as text with a dollar sign on purpose; parsing it is the cleaning task.
:::
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
::: {.etv-card}
### [top_films_backup.csv](data/top_films_backup.csv) · fallback for 03
The first table on Wikipedia's *List of highest-grossing films*, saved 2026-10-28 with its column names unchanged so the same cleaning code works on the live extract and on this file. 50 rows, 5 columns. Daggers (†) mark films still in theaters. Source: Wikipedia contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0.
:::
:::

## Before you arrive

Installs take 10–15 minutes and eat the hour if done live. Please finish these first. Full details are in [file 01](qmd/01_start_here_positron_and_r.qmd).

:::: {.grid}

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
### Pre-workshop checklist

1. Install **R 4.2 or newer** from [cloud.r-project.org](https://cloud.r-project.org/) (or with [rig](https://github.com/r-lib/rig)). Positron does not include R.
2. Install **Positron** from [positron.posit.co](https://positron.posit.co/download.html).
3. Open Positron once and confirm the interpreter selector (top-right) shows **R 4.x**.
4. Run the package installs on the right in the Console. Say yes to prompts.
5. Download the zip above, unzip it, and in Positron use **File → Open Folder…** on the `etv-workshop` folder.

Candy for the first correct prediction, the first fixed error, and the first plot.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
### Package installs (once per computer)

```r
# From CRAN
install.packages(c("readr", "dplyr", "ggplot2", "remotes"))

# htmltab was removed from CRAN on 2022-11-11,
# so it installs from the maintained GitHub fork:
remotes::install_github("htmltab/htmltab")

# Checkpoint: four TRUEs
c("readr", "dplyr", "ggplot2", "htmltab") %in%
  rownames(installed.packages())
```

Install once; load with `library()` at the top of every script.
:::

::::

## If something breaks

The four failures that eat workshop time. Each file has a longer troubleshooting list.

**`cannot open file 'data/cafe_orders.csv'`**
Wrong working directory. Run `getwd()`; it should end in `etv-workshop`. Use File → Open Folder… on that folder, then restart R.

**`package 'htmltab' is not available`**
Expected: it isn't on CRAN. Use `remotes::install_github("htmltab/htmltab")`. If GitHub rate-limits the room, skip it and use `top_films_backup.csv`.

**`could not find function "read_csv"`**
The package is installed but not loaded this session. Run `library(readr)`. Same fix for dplyr and ggplot2 functions.

**htmltab: table not found / columns look wrong**
Wikipedia changed the page. Try `which = 1`, or read the backup CSV; the column names match, so the rest of the code runs unchanged.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## About the code in these files
R code follows current readr, dplyr, and ggplot2 documentation but was not executed when these materials were built; expected outputs were computed from the CSVs separately. Each file lists what was and wasn't tested.
:::
